National Forest Carbon Monitoring, Accounting and Reporting System (NFCMARS) is designed to:

estimate past changes in forest carbon stocks, such as from 1990 to the present (monitoring)
predict changes in carbon stocks, based on scenarios of future disturbance rates and management actions, in the next 2 to 3 decades (projection)

title: Remote Sensing-based Yield Curves (RSYC) for Canada’s Forested Ecozones
text:
Existing models - limitations

there are over 100 Mha of forest for which we have no yield curves. And while we do not need to report on those forests, it is of great scientific interest to also quantify the C balance of those forests, as is the plan for the next generation system.  The curves developed in this project will enable national-scale coverage, inculding unmanaged forests

title: Remote Sensing-based Yield Curves (RSYC) for Canada’s Forested Ecozones
text:
Modeling


Model form after (Fortin and Lavoie 2022):
\[
AGB = \beta_1  e^{-\beta_4 age}  (1 - e^{-\beta_2  age})^{\beta_3}
\]
NLME:

random parameter: \(\beta_1\) (asymptote)
tile models: nested tile / pixel random effect
eco-strata models: nested ecozone / ecoprovince / ecoregion / ecodistrict / pixel random effects
one model per species (group) yields curves at all four ecological levels:


\[
\beta_{1,\text{ecodistrict}} = \beta_1 + b_{\text{ecozone}} + b_{\text{ecoprovince}} + b_{\text{ecoregion}} + b_{\text{ecodistrict}}
\]

Tiling & eco-stratification








150 × 150 km tiles – regular, spatially consistent modelling units








Nested ecological strata – ecozone → ecoprovince → ecoregion → ecodistrict

title: Remote Sensing-based Yield Curves (RSYC) for Canada’s Forested Ecozones
text:
Spatial units: eco-stratification


Example for black spruce and total volume, illustrating how the hierarchy works. From the ecozone level (e.g., Boreal Plains) down to ecoprovince (Boreal Foothills), ecoregion (Western Alberta Upland) and the individual ecodistricts. Curves become increasingly spatially specific, and separate more at finer levels. More detailed does not automatically mean better.

title: Remote Sensing-based Yield Curves (RSYC) for Canada’s Forested Ecozones
text:
Model library overview

Forest attribute: AGB, total volume
Species-specific or multi-species (Generic → Conifer / Broadleaf → Species)
Spatial representation: Tile, Ecozone → Ecoprovince → Ecoregion → Ecodistrict
Model formulation: National, Regional
Uncertainty


Two response variables; different levels of biological specificity; tiles plus the nested ecological hierarchy; national and regional formulations.

text:
Validation approach



Independent validation with national field plot data (MAGPlot)
Over 50,000 plots across Canada
Comparison by 20-year age classes









MAGPlot: harmonized national field-plot database, >50,000 plots from multiple jurisdictions. Observations are not distributed uniformly. Observations are summarized in 20-year age classes so heavily sampled ages do not dominate the assessment.

title: Remote Sensing-based Yield Curves (RSYC) for Canada’s Forested Ecozones
text:
Local calibration








One observation – a shrinkage-based level anchor, not a locally learned trajectory.








Several observations – more evidence for the local level while the age-dependent shape remains fixed.



Retain the age-dependent shape; adjust the local magnitude (BLUP of the pixel-level random effect on \(\beta_1\)).


Calibration alters magnitude, not growth shape. A single point informs a cautious BLUP adjustment. Several points provide stronger evidence. Neither case estimates a new temporal response.

text:

Curves are assigned to each pixel/segment and calibrated with the annual AGB observations, producing temporally consistent AGB trajectories.

Discover which models are available, predict by age, calibrate with local observations

Model parameters also available as plain CSV – usable outside R

title: Remote Sensing-based Yield Curves (RSYC) for Canada’s Forested Ecozones
text:
Model updates & versioning



Models updated on a two-year cycle, matching the NTEMS updates (new AGB, age and species time series)
Each release is explicitly versioned (e.g., v20260709 → v20260923)

model_version stored with every curve and in generated dataset metadata
stable model_id for every curve

Release notes document changes in coefficients and coverage
Parameters distributed as CSV with a checksum manifest; spatial boundaries versioned separately
Record model_id and model_version with any RSYC-derived product


Current release: v20260923

27,208 curves
corrected ecodistrict sampling
ecological models limited to the 12 forested ecozones
new numeric ecological strata codes (strata_code)
